group: HEART Score for Major Cardiac Events
question:
Patient note:
The 43-year-old female patient has no special history, and she has an annual check-up of computerized tomography to detect the mass in the right middle mediastinum, so the patient is admitted to the hospital. On-board examination, the patient was awake with good overall condition and has no abnormalities of the cardiovascular system and thoracic system during clinical examination. The manifestation on thoracic X-ray: right pulmonary hilum has an even, well-defined border (). Chest computerized tomography image showed a mass in the middle mediastinum with the size of 23 × 22.3 mm located between the right pulmonary artery and the pericardium with uniform margins and clear boundaries and did not invade the surrounding organization. A modest amount of contrast was absorbed after injection (). Echocardiography and respiratory function measurements were normal. Biochemical blood tests and complete blood count were in normal range. The preoperative diagnosis indicated that the tumor is located in the middle mediastinum with suspected mediastinal lymphadenopathy. The patient underwent uniportal video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery for tumor resection.
Operative procedure. We made a 3 cm skin incision on the VI intercostal space in the right anteriolateral side. The intraoperative examination found that the tumor of the right diaphragmatic nerve was about 2 × 3 cm in size () with clear tumor boundary to surrounding organs (including pericardium, pulmonary artery, and lung parenchyma), proving the noninvasiveness. We conducted a segmentation of the right phrenic nerve to remove the tumor and release the length of the phrenic nerve associated with reconnecting the right phrenic nerve with a prolene 8/0 through endoscopy (). The removed specimen was pale yellow with superficial hemorrhage (). Postoperatively, the patient was discharged after 4 days of treatment with a clinical condition of no difficulty breathing and no chest pain, and postoperative X-ray showed no abnormality; the right diaphragm was unchanged (). CT scanner result 1 month after discharge showed no abnormal images compared to the preoperative results ().

Question: What is the patient's score of the HEART Score? You should use the patient's medical values and health status when they were first admitted to the hospital prior to any treatment.
solution:
The HEART score assigns 0–2 points each for History, ECG, Age, Risk factors and Troponin in suspected acute coronary syndrome. This admission was for an incidental mediastinal mass, so the score is outside its usual setting.
- History: no ischemic symptoms described; low suspicion = 0.
- ECG: no admission ECG reported; assumed normal for this estimate = 0.
- Age: 43 years (<45) = 0.
- Risk factors: no coronary risk factors or known atherosclerotic disease documented = 0.
- Troponin: no specific result reported; assumed at or below the upper reference limit for this estimate = 0.
Conditional total: 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 = 0. The ECG and troponin components cannot be verified from the note.
Final answer: 0
